extracted.intended_audience: life-sciences researchers, manuscript authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors/publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for conducting and producing peer reviews of life-science manuscripts prior to journal submission (portable, journal-agnostic reviews intended to be reusable by journals and postable with preprints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific rigor and merit (journal-agnostic assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts will be assessed without regard to any journal to which they might ultimately be submitted, and will be judged exclusively for their scientific rigor and merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate the work on intrinsic scientific quality rather than subjective fit-for-journal criteria; the evaluation is intended to be independent of prospective journal audience or prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers will be asked to evaluate the technical rigor of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess methods, experimental design, analyses, data quality, reproducibility and validity of conclusions. Reviews should identify any technical flaws or weaknesses that affect the reliability of the results.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality, in-depth review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons aims to conduct high-quality, in-depth peer review of manuscripts before journal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be thorough and substantive so they provide a solid basis for authors to improve the manuscript and for editors to make informed decisions. Depth and quality are emphasized over cursory checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive suggestions for improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers will be asked to make suggestions for improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable, constructive feedback that helps authors address shortcomings (e.g., specific experiments, analyses, clarifications, or rewriting) rather than only listing problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of potential value to specific communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should comment on the potential value of the work to specific communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate relevance, applicability, and potential impact for particular subfields or user communities; note who would find the results important and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency through public posting of reviews and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can direct Review Commons to post reviews and their own response to bioRxiv through the Transparent Review in Preprints (TRiP) project, providing rich context for readers of the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare reviews with the expectation they may be made public alongside the preprint; include clear reasoning and sufficient context so readers can understand decisions and critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusability and sufficiency for editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons will facilitate transfer of the manuscript, reviews, and responses to affiliate journals; journals commit to use the Review Commons referee reports for their independent editorial decisions and to seek minimal additional expert input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write reports that are comprehensive and organized to allow editors to make efficient editorial decisions with minimal need for further re-review. Indicate remaining uncertainties or areas where journals might need additional input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission timing to reduce redundant reviewing and delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are performed before journal submission to reduce re-reviewing at multiple journals and accelerate publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct reviews early (pre-submission) and with sufficient completeness so authors can reuse the evaluation when submitting to journals, aiming to avoid repeated reviewer effort across successive submissions.
